subject: remote volcanic island
title: What If a Volcano Emptied the Most Remote Island on Earth? In 1961 It Did

scenes.text: What if a volcano woke under the most remote town on Earth? In 1961, 264 people found out.
Tristan da Cunha, South Atlantic. The nearest neighbours live on St Helena, about 2,400 kilometers away. Africa is six days by boat.
August 1961: tremors. October 9: a crack opens between the village and the fish factory. October 10: everyone boards two fishing boats and flees to a nearby islet.
A Dutch liner carried them to Cape Town, then a ship to England, arriving November 3. They were housed at a former airbase at Calshot.
The lava took the factory and the beach, but spared the village. In December 1962 the islanders voted: 148 to 5 to go home.
By November 1963 most were back, 2,400 kilometers from anyone. The volcano is still there. So are they.

description:
What if a volcano erupted beside the most remote inhabited settlement on Earth? On Tristan da Cunha in the South Atlantic, about 2,400 km from St Helena, tremors began in August 1961 and on 9 October a fissure opened between the village and the crawfish factory. On 10 October all 264 islanders and 31 expatriates left by fishing boat for Nightingale Island, then sailed to Cape Town and on to England.
The lava destroyed the factory and the beach but largely spared the village. In a secret ballot in December 1962 the islanders voted 148 to 5 to return, and the main party was home by November 1963.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: About a quarter of the islanders eventually chose to stay in Britain. Would you go back to a town with an active volcano next door?
